# 2\. Executive technical summary

Build one Next.js application containing the public pages, authenticated dashboard, and a versioned event API. Use Clerk for account sessions, Prisma for database access, and Neon PostgreSQL for persistent storage. Deploy the application on Vercel. Frontend and API share the same application origin; the submitting developer's backend calls the API using a project key.

Store every attributable outcome as a RequestRecord. An accepted record also represents the event, so accepted-event counts and accepted-request totals derive from the same committed row. No queue, separate ingestion server, Redis, browser collector, or event-processing worker is needed for the approved evaluation workload.

The database serializes event admission and key changes for each project. This ensures a key replacement and a concurrent submission have an explicit order, and the request limit remains effective across multiple function instances. Private dashboard reads bypass caches. A successful event response is sent only after the outcome is durably committed.

Allen approved these design decisions on 30 September 2026:

1\. Clerk account authentication with an owned production domain; actual domain provisioning and a spending ceiling remain deployment prerequisites.

2\. An exact rolling 30-day visible history window with daily physical cleanup and a maximum 25-hour deletion lag under normal operation. This approved clarification governs implementation where the source PRD's retention wording is less specific.

3\. The validation limits, rolling rate-limit semantics, test envelope, timeout and operational targets in this document. These are engineering acceptance targets, not measured results or a commercial SLA.

The design is approved for implementation planning. Provider setup, public-abuse controls and release evidence must be completed before public launch.

# 3\. Source PRD, scope, and constraints

The release must let a fresh public reviewer sign up, create multiple owned projects, issue one active key per project, submit a named event, and see both the event and its request outcome after refreshing within 30 seconds. It must support one-time key display, revocation/replacement, attributable errors, 60 submissions per minute per project, 30-day history, dark responsive screens, concise documentation, and public-URL release evidence.

Included Should requirements: first-use empty states, copy actions, replacement warning, and retention/data guidance. Also include the PRD's privacy notice and visible support/issue route before release.

Excluded: charts, event properties, client timestamps, end-user identity tracking, browser collection, SDKs, teams, invitations, billing, export, offline functionality, additional languages, and advanced filters. A separate admin product, automated account deletion UI, commercial SLA, and guaranteed delivery are not introduced.

Engineering assumptions: low-volume portfolio evaluation; one region near the selected Neon database; synchronous database writes; account ownership referenced by verified Clerk user ID without duplicating email/profile data. Neither visitor volume nor monthly budget is known. Section 13 contains a test envelope, not a traffic forecast. Docker is optional local learning infrastructure and is outside the required Vercel release path.

Allen confirmed no material change to the baseline on 30 September 2026. Familiar tools: Next.js, React, TypeScript/JavaScript, HTML/CSS, PostgreSQL/Neon, Prisma, Clerk, Git/GitHub and Vercel. Familiarity is not evidence that production security or operations are already verified.

# 7\. Architecture and decision record

The developer's backend and the user's browser cross distinct trust boundaries. Browser sessions authorize project management. API keys authorize only named-event submission for their associated project. The caller cannot supply a project ID to redirect attribution.

![System components and trust boundaries](data:image/png;base64,)

_Figure 1. System components and trust boundaries_

One module owns each trust-sensitive function: ownership, key authentication, ingestion, retention, and query-window calculation. Route Handlers translate HTTP into service calls and never duplicate ownership or admission rules. SQL required for locks, partial indexes and check constraints is stored in reviewed migrations or parameterized queries.

| **Decision**                | **Recommendation, rationale and tradeoff**                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| AD-01 Application topology  | One Next.js application. Fewer deployments and shared types; hot projects contend on one database row.                                     |
| AD-02 Authentication        | Clerk + owned domain, approved by Allen. Familiar workflow; domain/DNS setup is a release dependency \[S1\].                               |
| AD-03 Outcome/event storage | One RequestRecord table. Accepted rows are events; avoids partial event-versus-usage writes.                                               |
| AD-04 Admission             | PostgreSQL per-project lock + rolling admission query. Works across function instances; serialization limits throughput for a hot project. |
| AD-05 Consistency           | Commit before success; fresh reads, no private cache. Higher read cost but simple 30-second visibility.                                    |
| AD-06 Retention             | Exact read cutoff + daily deletion, with the approved deletion tolerance. Hobby scheduling does not provide frequent cleanup \[S2\].       |
| AD-07 Delivery              | No queue and no automatic ingestion retries. Lost responses may cause duplicate client submissions; delivery guarantees are excluded.      |
| AD-08 Docker                | Optional local PostgreSQL Compose environment or later container exercise. Not on the critical Vercel release path \[S7\].                 |

Important write sequence:

![Event ingestion transaction sequence](data:image/png;base64,)

_Figure 2. Event ingestion transaction sequence_

Verified secret is required before project attribution. Unknown keys stop before the transaction shown above. Section 12 defines outcomes that cannot be persisted during dependency failure.

# 9\. Data design

All identifiers below are UUIDs except Clerk user ID strings. Times are PostgreSQL timestamptz, represented as UTC ISO 8601 in HTTP. All fields are NOT NULL unless explicitly nullable. Generated IDs use cryptographically suitable platform/database UUID generation. Timestamps use server/database time, never user-supplied time.

![Project, key and request data relationships](data:image/png;base64,)

_Figure 3. Project, key and request data relationships_

CLERK_IDENTITY is an external logical identity, not a locally replicated database table or SQL foreign key.

| **Entity.field**                  | **Type, default/nullability**    | **Rules**                                                                        |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Project.id                        | uuid; generated                  | Primary key                                                                      |
| Project.ownerClerkUserId          | text; no default                 | Verified session identity only; indexed with createdAt,id                        |
| Project.name                      | varchar(80); no default          | Trimmed 1–80 characters; duplicate names allowed                                 |
| Project.createdAt                 | timestamptz; DB now              | Creation time                                                                    |
| Project.keyVersion                | integer; default 0               | Monotonic version incremented on each successful issuance/revoke/replace         |
| ApiKey.id                         | uuid; generated                  | Primary key; public credential lookup identifier                                 |
| ApiKey.projectId                  | uuid                             | FK Project; cascade on operator-authorized project deletion                      |
| ApiKey.secretHash                 | char(64)                         | SHA-256 hex of random secret; never store full key                               |
| ApiKey.displayHint                | varchar(48)                      | Public identifier/last secret characters only; never sufficient to authenticate  |
| ApiKey.createdAt                  | timestamptz; DB now              | Issuance time                                                                    |
| ApiKey.revokedAt                  | timestamptz; nullable            | NULL = active; otherwise permanently revoked                                     |
| RequestRecord.id                  | uuid; generated                  | requestId; accepted rows also use this as event id                               |
| RequestRecord.projectId           | uuid                             | FK Project                                                                       |
| RequestRecord.keyId               | uuid                             | FK ApiKey; composite FK (keyId,projectId) enforces key belongs to project        |
| RequestRecord.receivedAt          | timestamptz                      | Captured at service entry after bounded header processing; event arrival time    |
| RequestRecord.quotaAt             | timestamptz; nullable            | DB clock sampled after project lock; set only for an admitted active-key attempt |
| RequestRecord.outcome             | enum ACCEPTED,REJECTED           | One committed terminal outcome                                                   |
| RequestRecord.httpStatus          | smallint                         | 201 when accepted; specified 4xx for persisted rejection                         |
| RequestRecord.errorCode           | varchar(40); nullable            | NULL when accepted; stable code when rejected                                    |
| RequestRecord.eventName           | varchar(64); nullable            | Present only when accepted; no rejected raw payload stored                       |
| MaintenanceState.name             | text                             | Primary key; one row named retention                                             |
| MaintenanceState.lastSuccessAt    | timestamptz; nullable            | Updated after successful cleanup completion                                      |
| MaintenanceState.lastDeletedCount | bigint; default 0                | Non-sensitive operational statistic                                              |
| ManagementBucket.ownerClerkUserId | text                             | Composite primary key with operation and minuteStart; verified account identity  |
| ManagementBucket.operation        | enum PROJECT_CREATE,KEY_MUTATION | Shared across all owned projects for that operation                              |
| ManagementBucket.minuteStart      | timestamptz                      | Database UTC time truncated to the current minute                                |
| ManagementBucket.admittedCount    | integer; default 0               | Check 0–10; atomically increment only if below 10                                |

Constraints and indexes:

- Partial unique index ApiKey(projectId) WHERE revokedAt IS NULL; guarantees at most one active key.
- Unique ApiKey(id,projectId) supports the composite RequestRecord foreign key. RequestRecord.projectId also references Project directly.
- Check: accepted iff httpStatus=201, eventName is present, errorCode is NULL and quotaAt is present. Rejected rows have eventName NULL, a non-null errorCode and a supported 4xx status.
- RequestRecord(projectId,receivedAt DESC,id DESC), plus partial index for ACCEPTED rows; supports recent views and retained-window counts.
- Partial RequestRecord(projectId,quotaAt) WHERE quotaAt IS NOT NULL; supports rolling admission. RequestRecord(receivedAt,id) supports cleanup. Evaluate an extra (projectId,eventName,receivedAt) partial index only if query evidence warrants it.
- ApiKey(projectId,createdAt DESC,id DESC) supports key metadata. Partial/check constraints absent from the selected ORM schema syntax are created through SQL migrations and verified in integration tests.
- ManagementBucket(minuteStart) supports operational cleanup. Before a management mutation, atomically insert/increment its account/operation/minute bucket with a conditional upsert. If no slot is available, return 429 with Retry-After to the minute boundary. Consume the slot even if the subsequent mutation fails. This throttle is separate from the event quota.

Lifecycle: keys persist for the project lifetime, including revoked hashes, to verify and attribute genuinely revoked credentials. These are security metadata, not 30-day event history; replacement throttling limits gratuitous accumulation. Project records persist until an authorized operator processes a deletion/support request. RequestRecord rows are subject to the 30-day policy. Cleanup also removes ManagementBucket rows older than 25 hours; they are transient operational counters and do not appear in project usage. Routine operational logs never contain full keys, event payloads, or account emails.

No public project-delete endpoint is required by the PRD. The operator deletion runbook verifies the requesting identity, snapshots record counts without secrets, deletes the owned project's keys/outcomes in a transaction, and confirms its absence. Clerk account data is managed separately through the provider; deleting a Clerk identity alone does not automatically remove local projects. The privacy/support notice must explain this support process.

Migrations use an expand-first strategy. Add fields/indexes while old application code still works; backfill in bounded batches; switch reads/writes; remove obsolete fields only in a later release. Never execute reset, development migrations, or destructive schema synchronization against production.

# 10\. API and integration contracts

## 10.1 Common behavior

JSON responses use UTF-8 and UTC ISO timestamps. Owner APIs require a verified Clerk session and Project.ownerClerkUserId matching that identity. Authentication failure returns 401 JSON; an absent or foreign project returns identical 404 JSON. API keys never authorize these APIs. Management mutations require an allowed same-origin Origin and a CSRF-resistant session integration; GET routes do not mutate project/key data.

Disallowed/missing mutation Origin returns 403 ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED; an oversized management body returns 413. All management bodies are capped at 1 KiB. These common errors apply in addition to the endpoint-specific errors below.

Error envelope: {"error":{"code":"INVALID_EVENT_NAME","message":"Use 1–64 letters, digits or underscores, starting with a letter."},"requestId":"UUID"}. Field validation errors may add fields containing field names and safe messages, never the submitted secret/body. X-Request-Id carries the same ID. All private, issuance, ingestion and cleanup responses send Cache-Control: no-store. Standard framework 404/405 handling is normalized to safe API errors where applicable.

| **Method and path**                  | **Input and authorization**                        | **Success; errors**                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| GET /api/projects                    | Session; limit,cursor                              | 200 {items:\[{id,name,createdAt}\],nextCursor}; 401,400,503                                     |
| POST /api/projects                   | Session, allowed Origin; {name}                    | 201 {project}; 400,401,429,503                                                                  |
| GET /api/projects/:id                | Session and owner                                  | 200 {project,activeKey:{id,displayHint,createdAt} or null,keyVersion}; 401,404,503              |
| POST /api/projects/:id/keys          | Owner, Origin; {expectedKeyVersion}                | 201 {key:{id,value,displayHint,createdAt},keyVersion}; 400,401,404,409,429,503                  |
| DELETE /api/projects/:id/keys/:keyId | Owner, Origin; {expectedKeyVersion,confirmed:true} | 200 {revoked:true,keyVersion}; 400,401,404,409,429,503                                          |
| POST /api/projects/:id/keys/replace  | Owner, Origin; {expectedKeyVersion,confirmed:true} | 201 same issuance shape; 400,401,404,409,429,503                                                |
| GET /api/projects/:id/summary        | Owner                                              | 200 {window:{from,to,days:30},requests:{total,accepted,rejected},events:{total}}; 401,404,503   |
| GET /api/projects/:id/event-counts   | Owner; limit,cursor                                | 200 {window,items:\[{name,count}\],nextCursor}; 400,401,404,503                                 |
| GET /api/projects/:id/events         | Owner; limit,cursor                                | 200 {window,items:\[{id,name,receivedAt}\],nextCursor}; 400,401,404,503                         |
| GET /api/projects/:id/requests       | Owner; limit,cursor                                | 200 {window,items:\[{id,receivedAt,outcome,httpStatus,errorCode}\],nextCursor}; 400,401,404,503 |
| POST /api/v1/events                  | Bearer project key; {name}                         | 201 {event:{id,name,receivedAt},requestId}; error matrix below                                  |
| GET /api/internal/retention          | Bearer CRON_SECRET; no user input                  | 200 {deletedCount,completedAt}; 401,503                                                         |

Approved pagination rules: recent activity and project pages default 20, maximum 100; name/count pages default 50, maximum 100. Recent records sort receivedAt DESC,id DESC; projects createdAt DESC,id DESC; names alphabetically. Cursors encode a validated tuple, endpoint identity, project and snapshot upper timestamp; they do not confer authorization. Reject snapshot times in the future or older than the retained window. Every page rechecks ownership, rejects malformed/cross-endpoint cursors with 400, and applies the current retention cutoff. A record that expires between pages is omitted. No lifetime counters or chart series are returned.

The initial dashboard renders its totals and lists using one short database read transaction and one fixed read cutoff, so the visible panels agree. Later list pagination may show a newer snapshot; render the returned window. Summary invariant: requests.total = accepted + rejected and events.total = accepted. Grouped name counts sum to accepted over the same window when all pages are retrieved.

## 10.2 Project and key workflows

Create a project first, then explicitly issue its key using a prominent first-use action. If issuance fails, retain the project and let the owner retry. Duplicate create submissions may create duplicate named projects; names are not unique. Disable the submit control while pending and do not silently retry creation after an uncertain network result; refresh the list first.

Approved engineering baseline key format: ded_&lt;key-uuid&gt;.&lt;base64url-secret&gt;; secret is 32 cryptographically random bytes. Hash only that random secret with SHA-256; high-entropy API credentials are not human passwords. Lookup by public key UUID, decode the exact secret format, then compare the computed hash to the stored hash with a constant-time comparison. Wrong secrets, unknown IDs, missing/malformed headers return generic UNAUTHORIZED without attribution. A valid secret matching a revoked record returns KEY_REVOKED and is attributable.

Issuance/revocation/replacement lock the Project row, recheck ownership and expectedKeyVersion, and enforce active-key state. Initial issuance requires no active key; replacement requires an active key. Revoke marks the specified current key revoked and increments the version. Replacement revokes the old row and inserts the new row in one transaction, then increments the version. A competing action receives 409 KEY_STATE_CHANGED and refreshes state; a revoked key is never reactivated.

Display the full key only in the successful mutation response and transient panel. Never include it in GET, analytics, logs, URLs, browser local/session storage or cached HTML. Closing the panel/navigation clears it. Copy requires explicit action; guide examples retain a placeholder. A lost issuance/replacement response cannot recover the secret. Refresh the masked state and replace again through a new explicitly confirmed action. No automatic retry of a key mutation occurs.

## 10.3 Event validation and admission

Approved engineering baseline event contract: application/json; one strict object with exactly name; ASCII regex ^\[A-Za-z\]\[A-Za-z0-9_\]{0,63}\$; case-sensitive; do not trim or normalize names. Reject unknown properties, arrays, null, numbers, properties, user IDs and client timestamps. This matches the name-only PRD and makes validation predictable.

Bound headers and total body before parsing. Body limit approved at 1 KiB, enforced against streamed bytes even without Content-Length. Authorization header maximum 256 characters. Do not log body fragments. HTTP ingress/platform limits may reject traffic before application code; those responses cannot be guaranteed to have this application's envelope or attribution.

Approved engineering baseline project limit semantics: at most 60 **admitted active-key attempts** in any rolling 60 seconds. Invalid input with a verified active key consumes admission. A 429 attempt is recorded but does not extend the quota; revoked-key attempts do not consume active-key quota. The quota is shared by the project and survives key replacement. Missing/unknown keys have no project quota or project record. Allen approved this interpretation to specify the PRD's unspecified window and invalid-attempt counting behavior.

Service algorithm:

1\. Assign requestId and receivedAt; enforce bounded header/body reading. Verify the complete credential before attribution. Determine safe validation result outside the transaction; never hold a lock while reading a body or calling Clerk.

2\. Begin a short Read Committed transaction; lock Project by ID with SELECT FOR UPDATE. Re-read the key's project and revokedAt after acquiring the lock.

3\. If revoked, insert 401 KEY_REVOKED with quotaAt NULL. Otherwise sample database clock and count quotaAt strictly greater than clock minus 60 seconds. If 60 already exist, insert 429 RATE_LIMITED with quotaAt NULL; compute Retry-After from the oldest retained admission, rounded up, minimum one second.

4\. If below limit, set quotaAt and insert either the validation rejection or the accepted event/outcome. Commit before returning the response.

5\. On transaction failure, roll back and return 503 STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE where possible. Do not claim the request was accepted or successfully recorded.

All service paths affecting active key state or admissions acquire the same project lock in the same order. Admission time is sampled after waiting for the lock; using initial arrival time for quota checks would mishandle out-of-order concurrent requests. Raw SQL uses bound parameters \[S3,S4\].

An in-flight submission already admitted before replacement commits may succeed. After replacement/revoke returns success, every newly authenticated old-key submission must fail. This is the defined immediate-revocation boundary; requests are not retroactively erased.

## 10.4 Errors, attribution and examples

| **Condition**                                   | **Status/code**                          | **Linked project record**                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Missing, malformed, unknown key or wrong secret | 401 UNAUTHORIZED                         | No                                                            |
| Verified revoked key                            | 401 KEY_REVOKED                          | Rejected; no quotaAt                                          |
| Active verified key exceeds rolling admission   | 429 RATE_LIMITED + Retry-After           | Rejected; no quotaAt                                          |
| Invalid JSON                                    | 400 INVALID_JSON                         | Rejected with quotaAt when admitted                           |
| Missing/invalid name or extra fields            | 400 INVALID_EVENT_NAME / INVALID_PAYLOAD | Rejected with quotaAt when admitted                           |
| Unsupported content type                        | 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE               | Rejected with quotaAt when verified/admitted                  |
| Body exceeds application bound                  | 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE                    | Rejected if credential was verified and service can record it |
| Valid event                                     | 201                                      | Accepted with name and quotaAt                                |
| Database/transaction unavailable                | 503 STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE                  | Not guaranteed; operational log only                          |
| Platform/edge blocks, disconnects or timeout    | Provider-dependent                       | Not guaranteed; not presented as project usage                |

Authentication and revocation are evaluated before payload validation; rate admission precedes returning a payload error. The guide documents this precedence. Unknown credentials are never attributed from public key ID alone, so guessing an ID cannot pollute another project's usage.

Example request:

```
curl --request POST "$APP_URL/api/v1/events" \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $DED_API_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"name":"trial_started"}'
```

APP_URL is the deployed HTTPS origin; DED_API_KEY is temporarily set by the developer in their backend/terminal environment. The guide also provides a clearly labeled placeholder example. Do not place a real credential in source-controlled scripts or documentation.

Success example: {"event":{"id":"UUID","name":"trial_started","receivedAt":"2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z"},"requestId":"UUID"}; both IDs are identical for the accepted RequestRecord.

Idempotency: no ingestion deduplication, Idempotency-Key support or exactly-once delivery is included. Sending the same name twice creates two events. A commit followed by a lost response may leave the client unsure; retrying can duplicate an event. Check recent activity before retrying if avoiding duplication matters. Management actions also are not automatically retried. These limitations must appear in the guide.

Integration boundaries: Clerk session verification uses the pinned SDK and allowed origins. Neon operations use a pooling/driver configuration proven to support interactive transactions and row locks. No request to a third-party HTTP API occurs inside the ingestion transaction. Browser-side cross-origin collection is unsupported; do not enable a wildcard CORS policy. CORS is not credential protection: the key must stay in a developer's backend.

# 11\. Security and privacy

- Apply ownership checks in server services on every owner read and mutation; UI hiding and middleware alone are insufficient. Never accept owner ID from request JSON. Ingestion project ownership comes solely from a fully verified key.
- Use provider-managed account sessions; never store a custom session token in browser localStorage. Restrict authorized origins/parties and verify mutation Origin. Configure Clerk sign-up protections and production settings during SP-01.
- HTTPS for public traffic and TLS for PostgreSQL connections. Use runtime DB credentials without migration privileges where supported; migration credentials are restricted to the release operator/CI environment.
- Keep DATABASE_URL, migration credentials, CLERK_SECRET_KEY and CRON_SECRET server-side. Only Clerk's publishable key may use NEXT_PUBLIC_. No project secret is a public environment variable.
- Parameterize SQL; validate fields and pagination; escape rendered strings. No raw HTML rendering of project/event names. Never expose SQL errors, stack traces, connection strings or key hashes to users.
- Set appropriate CSP, anti-framing policy and nosniff headers, compatible with Clerk's required origins. Validate in production rather than guessing the provider allowlist.
- Approved supplemental public-abuse controls: authenticated project creation at most 10 admitted attempts per fixed UTC minute per account; key mutations at most 10 per fixed UTC minute per account. Use ManagementBucket as defined in Section 9. Unlike the event limiter, this control permits up to 20 attempts around a minute boundary. Authenticate and check Origin before consuming a management slot; test atomic admission across function instances in SP-02. Do not apply these limits to ordinary dashboard reads.
- Unknown-key flooding requires an upstream shared abuse control that operates before expensive database work. In SP-05 verify available hosting controls, trusted client-IP source, plan/cost and application-route exclusions; do not assume a paid firewall feature is included. Set a documented emergency ingestion kill switch. The project limiter cannot protect all traffic or unlimited 429 logging. If upstream protection is unavailable, approval of an alternate control is required before public launch.

Collect only a project name, verified owner identifier, key metadata, event name/arrival time and outcome metadata. Event names and project names can still contain personal information; instructions discourage this and validation does not guarantee absence of personal data. No compliance certification is asserted. Before launch, review geographic/provider processing and account/log/backup retention, and publish accurate privacy copy and a support route.

Record security-relevant key changes in redacted operational logs: requestId, project ID, actor ID, action, key ID/version, timestamp and result. Do not add a new user-facing audit feature. Determine and document provider log retention during release setup; do not describe runtime logs, authentication profiles or backups as covered by the 30-day event policy.

# 12\. Reliability and failure handling

| **Failure/state**                    | **User/system behavior**                                 | **Recovery and verification**                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Clerk unavailable                    | Show sign-in/session failure; deny owner operations      | Retry explicitly when service recovers; existing valid session verification tested; API ingestion does not call Clerk |
| DB unavailable                       | 503; show unavailable state, not empty/zero data         | Operational log; inspect DB connectivity; retry only after explicit user action                                       |
| Accepted insert or transaction fails | Roll back; never return 201                              | Verify no partial accepted row/count; T-09                                                                            |
| Commit succeeds but response is lost | Result uncertain; record may exist                       | Check dashboard; explain duplicate risk before resend                                                                 |
| Two key changes race                 | One succeeds; other 409                                  | Refresh masked state; require new confirmation                                                                        |
| Submit races with revoke             | Order by project lock                                    | Older admitted request may finish; later requests fail; T-05                                                          |
| Multiple function instances submit   | Shared DB rolling admission                              | Exactly 60 admitted from 61 concurrent valid attempts; T-08                                                           |
| Cleanup repeats/overlaps             | Safe bounded deletion; no live rows removed              | Transaction-scoped advisory lock or equivalent single-job coordination; idempotent cutoff predicates                  |
| Cleanup fails                        | Reads still hide expired rows; physical deletion overdue | Alert/check lastSuccessAt; invoke authenticated job after repair; never silently extend privacy claim                 |
| Pagination receives new writes       | Stable ordered tuple and snapshot upper bound            | Expired rows still excluded; validate cursor and authorization                                                        |
| Rate limit reached                   | Clear 429 and Retry-After                                | Client waits; no automatic immediate retry                                                                            |
| Browser offline/timeout              | Text error with retry; preserve unsent form value        | Never claim operation succeeded or replace real data with zero                                                        |

Approved engineering baseline transaction budget: lock timeout 2 seconds, statement timeout 3 seconds, total transaction timeout 5 seconds. Body read budget 3 seconds; bounded request handling aims to finish within 10 seconds with runtime headroom. Verify SDK/driver-specific timeout controls in SP-03; cancellation must release connections and transactions. No external network calls while holding locks. A transaction that has definitely rolled back due to a transient deadlock may be retried once within the remaining deadline; an ambiguous commit outcome is not automatically replayed.

Approved retention rules: at read time t, include receivedAt > t−30×24 hours and receivedAt ≤ t. Rows exactly at the lower boundary are expired. Display "Past 30 days"; format display time with an explicit timezone while storing UTC. Cleanup fixes a DB cutoff for that run and deletes receivedAt ≤ cutoff in batches of 1,000, up to 10,000 rows per invocation initially. If expired rows remain, log backlog and invoke again under operator control; tune batches within measured function limits. A successful completion updates MaintenanceState only when no expired rows remain at that fixed cutoff.

Daily cleanup at approved 02:00 UTC is compatible with the documented Hobby schedule. A 25-hour deletion-lag target applies only when the job and batch budget succeed; missed jobs are incidents, not an extension of the retention commitment. Hourly/minutely cleanup or a different scheduler changes plan/cost and requires a verified choice \[S2,S5\]. Backups can retain older copies under provider recovery policy; a restored database must run cleanup before serving user reads/writes. Privacy wording must distinguish live history from backup expiration.

# 13\. Performance, scalability and cost

| **Metric/constraint**             | **Target**                                                                        | **Status and method**                                                                                   |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Accepted-event refresh visibility | ≤30 seconds after 201                                                             | Confirmed; production timed check                                                                       |
| Project admission                 | 60 attempts/rolling 60 seconds                                                    | 60/min confirmed; rolling/error semantics approved                                                      |
| Visible event/request history     | Rolling 30×24 hours                                                               | 30 days confirmed; precise UTC cutoff approved                                                          |
| Physical cleanup lag              | ≤25 hours under normal operation                                                  | Approved PRD clarification; boundary and purge checks                                                   |
| Event payload/name                | ≤1 KiB; 1–64 ASCII characters                                                     | Approved engineering baseline; boundary and streamed-body tests                                         |
| Project name                      | 1–80 trimmed characters                                                           | Approved engineering baseline; form/API boundary tests                                                  |
| Pagination                        | 20 recent / 50 names default; maximum 100                                         | Approved engineering baseline; deterministic page/cursor tests                                          |
| Ingestion latency                 | Warm p95 ≤1 second; first idle request ≤10 seconds                                | Approved engineering baseline measurement goals, not SLA; same test region as hosting                   |
| Dashboard API latency             | Warm p95 ≤2 seconds                                                               | Approved engineering baseline; indexed-window fixture test                                              |
| Baseline load fixture             | 100,000 mixed outcome rows across 20 projects, including one with 50,000          | Approved engineering baseline evaluation envelope, not a forecast                                       |
| Load exercise                     | 10 concurrent clients, 5 aggregate requests/second for 2 minutes over 20 projects | Approved engineering baseline; schedule below each project's limit, plus separate 61-way boundary burst |
| Recovery exercise                 | Restore isolated dataset and resume valid flow within 2 hours of operator start   | Approved engineering baseline rehearsal goal; provider capability must be verified                      |
| Availability                      | Public core flow reachable at release                                             | Confirmed; no monthly uptime promise                                                                    |

No private response caching, materialized counters or separate analytics warehouse. Query retained windows using the indexes in Section 9; measure query plans before adding indexes. If volume exceeds the tested envelope, reassess before claiming capacity. At 60 accepted requests each minute for 30 days, one project alone could generate 2,592,000 admitted rows; rejected excess traffic adds more. Thus the per-project limit is not a global storage/cost cap.

During deployment, record actual plan usage/limits and set spending notifications where available. Allen must choose a monthly spending ceiling before enabling paid services. No free-tier capacity or restore entitlement is presumed. If the measured fixture exceeds provider limits, stop the load test, narrow the disclosed evaluation envelope or approve additional capacity; never silently drop accepted events.

Protect a public demo through upstream abuse controls, account-operation throttling, input bounds, cleanup and an operator ingestion kill switch. Additional hard project/storage quotas would alter product behavior and need a PRD decision; they are not added as an assumed feature.

# 14\. Observability and operations

Log structured requestId, route, HTTP status, duration, deployment/environment and stable error code. Add project/key/actor identifiers only when authenticated and necessary for diagnosis. Never log Authorization, Cookie, Clerk secret, DB URL, key plaintext/hash, raw event body or email. Store event content only in its intended database row.

Operational measures: application 5xx count, successful ingestion latency, rolling-limit rejections, DB timeout count, cleanup last success/backlog, migration version, and provider resource consumption. Project usage counts are user data derived from RequestRecord; they are not a substitute for operational outage monitoring.

Approved engineering baseline alert/check thresholds: investigate ≥5 storage/transaction errors in 5 minutes; failed fresh-account release smoke; ingestion p95 >2 seconds for a five-minute sampled exercise; or cleanup lastSuccessAt older than 26 hours. Low traffic means percentile signals may lack enough samples; do not fabricate an alert from missing data. Start with provider notifications and a repeatable manual health checklist; automated polling is optional unless needed to meet the chosen operational commitment. Do not create a reminder/automation as part of this design document.

Allen owns incidents. Investigation order: identify environment/deployment and request ID; inspect redacted app logs; check Clerk/Neon/Vercel status and config; reproduce with a disposable account/key; disable ingestion if privacy/security is at risk; use Section 17; capture resolution and retest. Cleanup incidents trigger authenticated purge and backlog verification. Key exposure requires revocation/replacement, never a rollback that reactivates a leaked key.

# 15\. Testing and verification

Use Vitest for validation/time/cursor and service unit tests; real isolated PostgreSQL integration tests for transactions, constraints and query behavior; Playwright for browser flows. Tools are approved and pinned during implementation. Mock-only tests do not prove database concurrency. CI uses disposable credentials/databases and redacted output. No test account passwords or project secrets enter the repository.

| **ID** | **Layer and meaningful evidence**                                                                                                                             | **Coverage**               |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| T-01   | E2E: fresh public sign-up → project → one-time key → documented curl → dashboard; sign-out                                                                    | FR-01–04,06,10; NFR-01,09  |
| T-02   | Integration/E2E: second account requests foreign list/detail/count/key/mutation paths; equal 404 behavior                                                     | FR-02; NFR-03              |
| T-03   | Integration/E2E: two projects, distinct names/keys/outcomes; selection/window state correct                                                                   | FR-03,08,09,12; NFR-03     |
| T-04   | Unit/integration/browser: random key format, hash-only DB, GET masking, no storage/log leaks, revisit clears panel                                            | FR-04; NFR-05              |
| T-05   | Integration: replace/revoke; old key fails, new succeeds; verified revoked outcome; submit race boundary                                                      | FR-05,07; NFR-03           |
| T-06   | Contract/E2E: 201 committed row; accepted name/count/outcome visible after refresh within 30 seconds                                                          | FR-06,08,09; NFR-02        |
| T-07   | Contract: invalid JSON/name/properties/type/size, missing key, unknown ID, known ID+wrong secret; safe errors and exact attribution                           | FR-07,09,10                |
| T-08   | Real DB concurrency: 61 active valid requests admit 60; malformed attempts consume quota; 429 does not extend window; boundary and replacement preserve quota | FR-11                      |
| T-09   | Fault injection: failed insert/commit, concurrent key mutation, transaction timeout; no false 201 or multiple active keys                                     | FR-04–07; reliability      |
| T-10   | Load: envelope in §13; no unexpected 5xx; visibility/latency evidence with region/cold-start conditions                                                       | NFR-02; approved targets   |
| T-11   | Clock/boundary + DB: just inside/exactly/outside 30 days; all APIs hide expired; cleanup deletes expired only; repeated/overlapping job; UTC/DST display      | NFR-04                     |
| T-12   | Browser: 360px and desktop; 200% zoom, keyboard, focus/dialog return, labels, contrast, reduced motion, pending/offline/error/empty states                    | FR-01,12; NFR-06,07        |
| T-13   | Security/content: auth bypass, CSRF Origin, SQL inputs, XSS strings, redaction, privacy/account/support/backup disclosures                                    | NFR-03,05,08               |
| T-14   | Release evidence: public URLs, fresh account, accepted/rejected/revoked/61st requests, two projects, guide/privacy/support, deployed scheduler and env review | NFR-01,09; PRD launch gate |
| T-15   | Migration/recovery: fresh DB and prior-version upgrade; old app compatible; restore isolated fixture, purge expired rows, smoke after recovery                | Deployment and rollback    |

Approved engineering baseline browser support: current stable desktop Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari; current stable Safari on iOS and Chrome on Android at release. Pin concrete version numbers in the release evidence. Playwright Chromium/Firefox/WebKit runs plus actual phone-browser smoke where accessible; emulation alone is recorded honestly and does not certify every device. If actual devices are unavailable, disclose that evidence gap and revise the release support claim.

Retention fixtures use test-only injected clocks for read-window logic and seeded timestamps in a disposable database; production clock cannot be changed through a public API. Test cleanup with expired rows now rather than waiting 30 days. Also observe at least one real deployed scheduled invocation. Capture build SHA, environment, date, expected/result, latency/visibility measurement and redacted screenshots/output. Do not claim checks passed before collecting evidence. Optional independent usability review remains optional as the PRD states.

# 16\. Deployment and rollout

| **Environment** | **Database/auth/config**                                                             | **Purpose**                                      |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Local           | Disposable local PostgreSQL or Neon development database; Clerk development instance | Develop and unit/integration checks              |
| Preview         | Isolated Neon preview database; Clerk development/test-compatible setup              | Branch review; never production data/credentials |
| Production      | Dedicated Neon production database; Clerk production instance and owned domain       | Public evaluator flow                            |

No additional staging service is necessary for this portfolio baseline. Production authentication must be tested separately because its domain/credentials differ. A preview with development authentication is not production-equivalent.

| **Configuration**                 | **Exposure and intended value**                                                                              |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| APP_URL                           | Server configuration; canonical local/preview/production origin; production is final HTTPS domain            |
| NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY | Browser-safe provider key; correct instance per environment                                                  |
| CLERK_SECRET_KEY                  | Secret; never NEXT_PUBLIC_; matching provider instance                                                       |
| DATABASE_URL                      | Secret runtime connection; environment's pooled/adapter-compatible DB                                        |
| MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL            | Secret migration-role connection; load through pinned Prisma config/CI job; not a assumed magic ORM variable |
| CRON_SECRET                       | Random server secret; scheduler bearer authorization; independent by environment                             |
| INGESTION_ENABLED                 | Server-only kill switch; true normally; false returns 503 before event processing                            |

Clerk path/redirect variables are added only as required by the selected SDK configuration. Store local secrets in ignored env files; commit .env.example with placeholders. Validate required configuration at startup/build as appropriate. Environment updates apply to subsequent deployments; changing a setting does not itself validate or publish the app \[S6\]. Build-time browser configuration must be rebuilt for its target environment; avoid blindly promoting a preview compiled with test auth keys.

CI: clean install from lockfile; formatting/lint/type checks; unit/contract tests; real PostgreSQL integration and migration tests; production build. Preview deployment then browser smoke. Scan for accidentally committed secrets and investigate actionable dependency vulnerabilities; do not rely on a scanner alone to prove safety. No destructive test or load traffic runs against real production data.

Ordered rollout/checklist:

1\. **Prepare:** approve design/domain/retention; pin versions; create isolated resources; document owner and costs. Record current production config and known-good build.

2\. **Deploy early (Weeks 1–2):** landing, guide shell, auth/project flow at production URL; finish production DNS/credentials; fresh-account gate.

3\. **Database first:** review additive migration, test on prior-version fixture, verify backup/restore capability, execute production migration once through controlled release job/operator. Do not migrate from arbitrary preview build scripts.

4\. **Deploy application:** use production-scoped credentials/config; build for production; publish with compatible schema. Keep emergency ingestion disabling available.

5\. **Activate cleanup:** verify CRON_SECRET, path, production schedule and actual authenticated run; preview cleanup never targets production. Confirm cron endpoint is public to the scheduler but secret protected.

6\. **Run release gate:** T-01 through applicable T-15 with fresh accounts and public API. Check unauthenticated clients are not blocked by deployment protection. Confirm support route and final documentation.

7\. **Observe:** run sampled production smoke and inspect redacted errors/cleanup health; archive build SHA, URLs and results. Announce portfolio availability only after the launch gate passes.

Go/no-go: no cross-account/project access; exactly one active key; no secret leakage; valid event visible within 30 seconds; specified rejected outcomes; verified 60/minute semantics; visible and physical retention meets approved policy; public signup/docs work; mobile/keyboard flow usable; migration and recovery rehearsal passed. Any failed Must requirement blocks release. No feature-flag platform is needed; INGESTION_ENABLED provides a narrow incident control rather than adding product scope.

# 17\. Rollback runbook

| **Step**                       | **Operator action and success criterion**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1\. Contain                    | Allen records incident/build/config and request IDs. Disable ingestion when corruption or secret/tenant exposure is suspected; suspend faulty cleanup if it could delete live data. Verify maintenance/error response.                                                                                                                   |
| 2\. Select safe build          | Identify the last verified application build that works with the current additive schema. Avoid blindly rolling back to code incompatible with new data.                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 3\. Restore application        | Roll back/redeploy the selected build. Verify the actual production alias/domain and target-environment configuration. Environment kill-switch changes may require a fresh deployment.                                                                                                                                                   |
| 4\. Restore configuration      | Reapply the known-good non-secret values; recover secret versions through authorized secret controls. Never restore a compromised project/provider secret just to match an older build. Rebuild browser config if changed.                                                                                                               |
| 5\. Inspect scheduler          | Confirm active cron path/schedule, secret and code match the intended safe deployment. Verify actual state after platform rollback and reconfigure if needed \[S5\].                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 6\. Handle schema/data         | Leave harmless additive migrations in place. Prefer a tested forward fix. For corrupt/destructively changed data, restore to a separate Neon database from verified backup/recovery capability; validate ownership/key rows, rerun cleanup, then switch connection and deploy. Never run an untested down migration or reset production. |
| 7\. Preserve credential safety | A restore may reintroduce formerly active leaked keys. Reapply revocations from the incident record or invalidate affected project keys before reopening ingestion. New valid events since restore point may be lost; record the actual recovery point and inform affected users where relevant.                                         |
| 8\. Third-party state          | Verify Clerk production domain, redirect settings and credentials independently. Application rollback does not undo provider/DNS changes. Use recorded settings and provider guidance; account for propagation.                                                                                                                          |
| 9\. Reopen                     | Fresh-account sign-in, two-project isolation, accepted event, revoked-key denial, limit and retention checks pass. Re-enable ingestion/cleanup through deployment and verify public responses. Record cause, impact and follow-up.                                                                                                       |

Neon plan recovery features and recovery window are not presumed. Before release, demonstrate either provider recovery or a documented encrypted backup/restore path in a disposable environment. Record achievable recovery point and duration; a successful app rollback alone does not prove data recovery. Retained backups and recovery artifacts have separate access/expiration controls.

# 18\. Implementation plan

The PRD's eight weeks at five hours/week is the baseline. Suggested allocations total 40 hours; spikes are included, not extra. If a gate fails or work exceeds its allocation, revise the timeline with Allen instead of dropping Must requirements or verification.

| **Weeks / budget** | **Work package and dependencies**                                                                                                                     | **Exit gate**                                                                                                         |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1–2 / 10 hours     | WP-01 approve consequential decisions; SP-01/SP-05; repository, env isolation, schema foundation, landing/auth/project flow; early public deploy      | Fresh production account creates/selects project; second account denied; config/version record exists                 |
| 3–4 / 10 hours     | WP-02 SP-02/SP-03; key lifecycle, transaction services, basic validation and rolling admission; accepted ingestion and initial fresh dashboard read   | Public documented first event visible within 30 seconds; hash-only key and concurrency gates pass                     |
| 5–6 / 10 hours     | WP-03 retained counts/lists/usage; full rejected outcomes; revoke/replace UI; guide/privacy/support; SP-04 and cleanup; supplemental abuse controls   | Two-project separation, old-key denial, 61st response, attributable errors, retention fixtures and scheduled run pass |
| 7–8 / 10 hours     | WP-04 accessibility/mobile states; complete CI/E2E/security/migration/load checks; recovery rehearsal; documentation and redacted release walkthrough | Full launch gate and owner release decision with evidence                                                             |

Definitions of done: user behavior works through public URLs; ownership and error rules implemented once in server services; constraints/migrations reproducible; contracts/docs match actual responses; tests and evidence mapped to requirements; no committed credentials; rollout/rollback instructions reproducible. Docker exercises and nonessential visual polish follow completion of these gates. This plan is tight for 40 hours; the most likely schedule pressure is production auth, concurrency, retention and recovery, not additional UI features.

# 19\. Risks, decisions and open questions

| **Risk**                                            | **Impact / control / decision owner**                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Domain/Clerk setup repeats prior deployment failure | High. Approve owned domain path and prove real production signup in Weeks 1–2. Allen.                                            |
| Daily purge conflicts with strict 30-day wording    | High. Approve explicit deletion tolerance or choose verified more frequent scheduler; do not silently weaken NFR-04. Allen.      |
| Public abuse exceeds project limiter                | High. Verify upstream shared abuse controls, management throttles, spending notifications and kill switch before release. Allen. |
| Concurrent requests bypass limit/revocation         | High. Single project lock, DB constraints and real concurrency tests. Allen.                                                     |
| Secret lost or leaked                               | High. Hash-only storage, response-only display, no replay, explicit replacement and redaction tests. Allen.                      |
| ORM/driver mismatch breaks transactions             | High. Pin supported versions and prove chosen driver/lock semantics before service implementation. Allen.                        |
| Full 30-day volume exceeds evaluation envelope      | Medium/high. Measure, disclose tested capacity, monitor provider limits; additional quotas/capacity require decision. Allen.     |
| Recovery resurrects expired history/revoked keys    | High. Cleanup and revocation reconciliation before restored service opens. Allen.                                                |
| 40-hour schedule insufficient                       | High. Evidence-based weekly gates; extend timing if necessary; no unapproved requirement removal. Allen.                         |

Approved decisions, 30 September 2026:

- **D-01:** Clerk production with owned domain, subject to separately established spending limit. Provision and verify the production domain before the first public authentication gate.
- **D-02:** 30-day visibility plus daily purge with ≤25-hour normal-operation lag; approved clarification of PRD retention wording; align deployed privacy and guide copy. Daily cleanup must meet this tolerance; any different policy requires a reviewed design change.
- **D-03:** Approved engineering baseline validation, rolling-limit interpretation, timeout/load/performance and recovery test targets.

Release blockers to close during implementation: actual domain/DNS/provider configuration; upstream abuse-control choice; provider costs and monthly budget; production browser versions/evidence; privacy/support destination and account/log/backup policies; restore capability/recovery window; deployed scheduler invocation. These do not require speculative product features; they require concrete setup and verification.

Design review: all material PRD requirements and included Should items map to components and verification. Architecture, data, contracts, security, concurrency, retention, performance, operations, deployment and recovery are specified. Allen approved D-01–03 on 30 September 2026. Public release remains conditional on the setup and verification gates above.

# 20\. Appendices

## Glossary

| **Term**             | **Meaning**                                                                                   |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Authentication       | Prove an account session or API credential is valid                                           |
| Authorization        | Decide which project operations that identity/credential may perform                          |
| Attributable request | Request whose full key secret matches a known project key, including a revoked key            |
| Accepted event       | Committed ACCEPTED RequestRecord containing a valid event name and service arrival time       |
| Rolling window       | Interval measured backward from the current server/database time, not a calendar month/minute |
| Transaction          | Database work that commits together or rolls back together                                    |
| Row lock             | Database coordination that orders concurrent changes to one project                           |
| Logical expiration   | Expired records cannot appear in product reads/counts                                         |
| Physical cleanup     | Expired rows are deleted from the live database                                               |
| Preview              | Isolated branch deployment used to review a change                                            |
| Production           | Public evaluator environment using final production resources                                 |

## Primary technical references

Sources checked on 30 September 2026. Provider behavior/plan terms must be rechecked during setup if they change. References support platform facts; the architecture and approved limits are project design decisions.

- **S1 — Clerk production deployment:** <https://clerk.com/docs/guides/development/deployment/production> . Production setup requires an owned domain/DNS access, appropriate instance credentials, and provider-specific setup.
- **S2 — Vercel cron usage:** <https://vercel.com/docs/cron-jobs/usage-and-pricing> . Hobby scheduling is daily with hour-level timing; more frequent scheduling depends on plan.
- **S3 — Prisma transaction reference (v7):** <https://docs.prisma.io/docs/orm/v7/prisma-client/queries/transactions> . Short transactions, isolation and timeout options; syntax is version dependent.
- **S4 — PostgreSQL row locks:** <https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/explicit-locking.html> . FOR UPDATE coordinates concurrent changes until the transaction ends.
- **S5 — Vercel cron management:** <https://vercel.com/docs/cron-jobs/manage-cron-jobs> . Secret authorization, scheduling behavior and rollback management.
- **S6 — Vercel environment variables:** <https://vercel.com/docs/environment-variables> . Environment scoping and deployment application of values.
- **S7 — Next.js self-hosting:** <https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/self-hosting> . Container/self-hosting is an alternative delivery path; Vercel remains this design's approved host.
- **S8 — Next.js Route Handlers:** <https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route> . HTTP methods, response handling and version-sensitive route conventions.
